# firecrawl crawl

Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

**Prerequisite:** `crawl` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Crawl a docs section
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --include-paths /docs --limit 50 --wait -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Full crawl with depth limit
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --max-depth 3 --wait --progress -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Check status of a running crawl
firecrawl crawl <job-id>
```

Run `firecrawl crawl --help` for the full option list.

**Done when:** the crawl reaches a terminal status and the saved output under `.firecrawl/` contains the expected pages.

## Tips

- Use `--wait` when you need the results immediately. It has no default timeout; use `--timeout <seconds>` to bound polling. Without `--wait`, crawl returns a job ID for async polling.
- **Scope crawls with `--include-paths`** whenever the request names a section — crawl only the pages you need.
- Crawl consumes credits per page. Check `firecrawl credit-usage` before large crawls (`credit-usage` requires authentication).

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs before deciding to crawl
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download site to local files (uses map + scrape)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

"

"

The crawl returned 10 pages (the cap). The full output is saved at `/tmp/fceval-s07-t1-ig5ob73h/work/.firecrawl/crawl.json`.

1. **`/features`**: The URL for this page returned content about SSO and SCIM (SAML/OIDC sign-in plus automatic user and group provisioning), an enterprise feature.
2. **`/features/llm-extract`**: JSON-mode extraction pulls structured fields from a single URL with a schema. For multiple URLs or agentic discovery, use Agent instead.
3. **`/features/alpha/deep-research`**: This is the legacy v1 Deep Research API. It is deprecated in favor of Search, and Firecrawl stopped maintaining it after June 30, 2025.
4. **`/features/research`**: Firecrawl Research is a paper index of about 43M abstracts, mostly PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv and arXiv. It supports search, metadata, passage reading and related-paper discovery.
5. **`/features/threat-protection`**: This lets an organization block risky URLs. Every fetch is checked against the org's policy, whether it comes from a scrape, search, crawl or agent request.
6. **`/features/ask`**: `/support/ask` is an AI support agent exposed as an API. It returns a diagnosis with fix parameters in about 15–30 seconds, and is aimed at agent callers.
7. **`/features/research.md`**: This is the markdown version of the Research page (item 4), so it duplicates that page.
8. **`/features/pii-redaction`**: Setting `redactPII: true` on a scrape replaces personally identifiable information in the returned markdown before it goes downstream.
9. **`/features/proxies`**: The `proxy` parameter selects the proxy type for sites of varying difficulty, and location-based selection is supported. Requests go through proxies by default.
10. **`/features/ip-restrictions`**: This is a team-level allowlist of IPs and CIDR ranges, enforced server-side on every API request. It makes a leaked key useless outside approved networks, and it is an enterprise feature.

The 10-page cap was filled before the crawl reached other pages under `/features`, such as scrape, search, crawl and agent. Items 1 and 7 are also oddities. The base `/features` URL returned SSO content, and the `.md` variant is a duplicate. If you want, I can re-run with a different path filter to cover the core feature pages.
